statement.p: A fluid moves through a tube of length 1 meter and radius r = 0.004 \pm 0.00015 meters under a pressure p = 3\cdot 10^5 \pm 2000 pascals, at a rate v= 0.75 \cdot 10^{-9} \hbox{m}^3 per unit time. Use differentials to estimate the maximum error in the viscosity \eta given by \eta = \frac{ \pi}{8} \frac{p r^4}{v}.

static.solution:
\eta is approximated by d\eta, where d\eta = \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial r} dr + \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial p} dp.
We need to find \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial r}=\frac{ \pi}{8} \frac{p 4 r^3}{v } and \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial p}=\frac{ \pi}{8} \frac{ r^4}{v}. For r = 0.004, v = 0.75\cdot 10^{-9} and p=3\cdot 10^5 we get \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial r}(0.004,3\cdot 10^5) = \frac{ \pi}{8} \frac{(3\cdot 10^5)(4\, (0.004)^3)}{0.75\cdot 10^{-9}} = 4.02124\times 10^{7}, and similarly \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial p}(0.004, 3\cdot 10^5) = 0.134041, so that d\eta = \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial r} d r + \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial p} dp. is largest when we take all positive values to give d\eta = (4.02124\times 10^{7})(0.00015) + (0.134041)(2000) = 6299.94.
This seems quite large, but \eta(0.004,3\cdot 10^5) = 40212.4, so the maximum error represents about 20 % of any value computed by the given formula. Notice also the relative error in r is \pm 4 %, which means that the relative error in r^4 is \pm 10 %.
